narrative:
You will take remedial courses because the model estimates you have a 12 percent chance of not passing your final year. You are still more likely to succeed than not, but the school treats risk at this level seriously, so the courses are a precaution rather than a verdict.

The three strongest influences on your prediction all actually lower your risk. Most important is why you chose this school: because of its reputation. Students who choose a school for that reason tend to be more motivated, and this pattern is common among students who passed. Second, you have no past class failures. That clean record is a strong sign you know how to succeed, and students who passed also averaged zero previous failures. Third, you described your family relationships as good. That stable home support helps your studies, and most students who passed reported good or very good family relations.

So why does the model still flag you? Because smaller factors are pulling the other way. Your health is very bad, your free time is very high, you go out with friends often, and your weekend alcohol consumption is medium. None is dramatic alone, but together they offset your strengths.

To improve your chances, treat the remedial courses as a tool. Focus on your health, reduce weekend drinking, and turn some free time into structured study time. Small changes can make a real difference.
